clue.text: Burned money in sack

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is held inside it, so the money sits within the sack

parts.note: to hit the sack is to go to bed, so sack stands for bed
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: Someone has set fire to a sack of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Every across clue with 'money' hides a different currency; here it is South Africa's, tucked inside B...ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle are branded by burning a mark into the hide with a hot iron, so branded means burned.

clue.text: A truce FBI violated in split

indicators.note: a violated agreement is broken, so these letters are broken up and reset

parts.note: the nine letters of these three words, rearranged

explanation.surface: The FBI breaks a ceasefire and causes a rift.
explanation.definitionFit: To bifurcate is to fork into two branches, which is to divide or split.

clue.text: Frighten nearly every member

indicators.note: nearly the whole word means it falls one letter short at the end

parts.note: every one of them is all of them
a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: Scare almost all of the club's members.
explanation.walkthrough: Member means a limb of the body here, not someone in a club.
explanation.definitionFit: To alarm someone is to startle them with fear, which is to frighten them.

clue.text: What's proper in 1930s-style liquor?

parts.note: Art Deco was the design style of the 1920s and 1930s
rum is a liquor distilled from sugarcane

explanation.surface: A query about etiquette in the cocktails of the Prohibition era.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is correct, polite behaviour, the conduct society considers fitting.

clue.text: Trickle-down: rest in peace

parts.note: d is a standard abbreviation for down
RIP is the abbreviation carved on gravestones

explanation.surface: A gloomy joke that trickle-down economics deserves to be buried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trickle-down' reads as the economic theory, but the hyphen splits it into the definition and a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A drip is a small falling drop of liquid, and to drip is to trickle slowly.

clue.text: Smacked lips very loudly with a joint

indicators.note: something smacked is knocked about, so the letters of the next word are knocked out of order

parts.note: the four letters of lips, rearranged
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone noisily smacks their lips while enjoying a smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smacked lips' reads as one action, but smacked is the signal to rearrange lips.
explanation.definitionFit: A spliff is slang for a hand-rolled cannabis cigarette, which is also called a joint.

clue.text: Woman promoted inane tech company

indicators.note: in a down clue being promoted moves the letters upward, so they read from the bottom

parts.note: inane and silly both mean foolish
HP is Hewlett-Packard, the computer maker

explanation.surface: A woman gets a promotion at a pointless technology firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Phyllis is a woman's given name, and crosswords often define a name simply as woman.

clue.text: Skipping the onset of champions' cheer to find part of a shoe

indicators.note: to skip the onset of a word is to leave out its first letter

parts.note: champions are winners
olé is the cheer of a bullfight crowd

explanation.surface: Fans miss the start of the victory chant.
explanation.definitionFit: The innersole is the layer inside a shoe on which the foot rests, also called the insole.

clue.text: Spoken idiom gets worn out

indicators.note: a spoken word is heard rather than seen, so the sound matters, not the spelling

parts.note: an idiom is a set phrase

explanation.surface: A saying gets tired from overuse.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a hackneyed expression; the answer is a verb meaning to wear thin at the edges.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric that frays wears away into loose threads, so it is worn out by use.

clue.text: Poem: "Cutting Into Fruit With Instrument"

indicators.note: something cutting into another thing goes inside it

parts.note: a melon is a fruit
an ode is a poem

explanation.surface: It reads like the title of a poem about slicing fruit with a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals dress the clue as a poem's title, and instrument looks like a knife; it is the musical kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodeon is a small reed organ or button accordion, a musical instrument.

clue.text: Money leads to that man's enthusiasm to start a business

parts.note: the franc was the currency of France and is still used in Switzerland
the possessive of he

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the beginning of enthusiasm is kept

parts.note: the first letter of enthusiasm

explanation.surface: Cash fires up a man's urge to launch his own company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To start a business' looks like the definition, but 'to start' only takes the first letter of enthusiasm; the definition is just 'a business'.
explanation.definitionFit: A franchise is a licensed outlet trading under a parent brand, such as a fast-food restaurant, so it is a kind of business.

clue.text: Gossip from graduate student going after money

indicators.note: going after places the student behind the money in the sequence

parts.note: the yen is the currency of Japan
a TA, teaching assistant, is a graduate student who helps teach a course

explanation.surface: A rumour spread by a grad student chasing cash.
explanation.walkthrough: TA for teaching assistant is the usual American term for a graduate student who teaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Yenta is a Yiddish-derived word for a busybody, a person who gossips and meddles.

clue.text: Make an observation about money

parts.note: re means concerning, as at the top of a memo
the mark was the currency of Germany before the euro

explanation.surface: Someone comments on the subject of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark is to say something you have noticed, which is a spoken observation.

clue.text: The first unit of money sent back in 100s (they're green)

indicators.note: placed in the hundreds, so the moved word sits between them
picks out the opening letter of the word that follows, the one to be moved
sending that letter to the back moves it from the front of the word to its end

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, so two of them are Cs
the dollar is the currency of the United States

explanation.surface: A tidy count of greenbacks, the parenthesis hinting at the colour of dollar bills.
explanation.walkthrough: The D of the money moves to its end, and the result goes between C and S. The parenthesis looks like an aside about banknotes but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Collards, collard greens, are a leafy cabbage vegetable eaten in the American South, so they are greens.

clue.text: Basic principle: cut ten meters

parts.note: to ax is to cut, in the American spelling
ten written as the digits 1 and 0, which look like the letters I and O
m is the symbol for meters

explanation.surface: A rule about trimming something by ten meters.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a self-evident truth taken as a starting point for reasoning, a foundational principle.

clue.text: Snoopy's fashionable comic virtues

indicators.note: something comic is played for laughs and out of joint, so the next word is reset

parts.note: what is fashionable is in
the seven letters of virtues, rearranged

explanation.surface: The cartoon beagle Snoopy shows off his stylish, funny good qualities.
explanation.walkthrough: Snoopy and comic suggest the Peanuts strip; here snoopy just means nosy, and 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone snoopy pries into others' business, and intrusive describes exactly that prying.

clue.text: Physicist prepares to pray with someone tiresome on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so the spelling is chosen by sound

parts.note: getting down on your knees before praying
a tiresome person is a bore

explanation.surface: A scientist kneels in prayer beside a dull companion during a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danish scientist Niels Bohr modelled the atom and won the 1922 Nobel Prize in Physics.

clue.text: Most clangorous thing that's charged up cut short nap

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: a siesta is an afternoon nap

explanation.surface: A battery charged up interrupts a nap with a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Clangorous means loud and ringing, so the most clangorous thing makes the most noise.

clue.text: Honorable creed: "Step lively!"

indicators.note: a lively dance moves things around, so these letters are set moving into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A noble motto that boils down to 'hurry up!'.
explanation.definitionFit: An honorable person is held in high esteem, which is to be respected.

clue.text: Reach sixteen? No, that's ridiculous

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurd and out of order, so the preceding letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of turning sixteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reach sixteen' reads as one phrase about a birthday; reach is the definition and stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Reach and extension both mean how far something stretches out, as in the reach of a law.

clue.text: Tip O'Neill has plentiful quantities of pasta

parts.note: surface padding: only the Irish prefix of the Speaker's surname, completing his name

indicators.note: the tip of something is its very end, here the leading letter

parts.note: the first letter of Neill
oodles means lots

explanation.surface: Tip O'Neill, longtime Speaker of the US House, has lots of spaghetti.
explanation.walkthrough: Tip O'Neill was the famous Speaker of the US House; his nickname is borrowed here to take the first letter of Neill.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles are strips of pasta, as in egg noodles.

clue.text: Emphasize missing front lock

indicators.note: a word missing its front has lost its first letter

parts.note: to stress something is to emphasize it

explanation.surface: An instruction to underline the absence of a front lock on a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door, but here it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long curl of hair, just as a lock is a strand of hair.

clue.text: Greek character kidnaps uncouth prime minister

indicators.note: a kidnapper holds the victim inside, so one word is held within another

parts.note: tau is the Greek letter T
uncouth and rude both mean ill-mannered

explanation.surface: A boorish head of government is abducted by a Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre Trudeau, and later his son Justin, served as Canada's prime minister.

clue.text: Money separates nephew's opening from sib, resulting in disorder

indicators.note: to separate two things you stand between them, so the money goes in the middle
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of nephew
the euro is the currency of most of the European Union
a sis is a sister, one kind of sib or sibling

explanation.surface: A family quarrel: cash comes between a nephew and his sibling, and chaos follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosis is a mental disorder marked by anxiety or obsessive behaviour.

clue.text: Bad grade at English school raised and recorded

indicators.note: in a down clue raising letters means reading them upward

parts.note: D is a poor grade on an American report card
Eton is England's famous boarding school

explanation.surface: A poor mark at a posh school is brought up and written down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noted has been written down, which is to say recorded.

clue.text: Money conceals trace of bomb debris

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hold it hidden inside

parts.note: the ruble is the currency of Russia

indicators.note: a trace is the smallest hint of something, so just its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of bomb

explanation.surface: Cash hides any sign of the bomb's wreckage.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubble is broken stone and brick left after a building collapses, a kind of debris.

clue.text: Howard is in British Columbia with a horse

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: BC is the postal abbreviation for the Canadian province of British Columbia
Ron Howard is the actor and film director

explanation.surface: A man named Howard is out in western Canada on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: Howard is a surname here; the first name of the director Ron Howard is what goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronc, short for bronco, is an untamed horse of the American West.

clue.text: Very animated course

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
up means lively and in high spirits

explanation.surface: A description of a lively cartoon film or class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animated course' suggests a cartoon or a lively lesson; course is a part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Soup is served as one course of a meal, usually the first.

clue.text: Originally, the money is a challenge

indicators.note: what something was originally is how it began, so only its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the
the rial is the currency of Iran and Oman

explanation.surface: Getting the cash in the first place is the hard part.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is a test of endurance or ability, something that challenges you.

clue.text: Money carried by one who reconnoiters and examines

indicators.note: what is carried by someone is held inside their grasp, so the money goes within

parts.note: a scout goes ahead to reconnoiter
the peso is the currency of Mexico and several other countries

explanation.surface: A spy carries the cash while surveying enemy ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To scope out is an informal phrase for to look over or investigate, which is to examine.

clue.text: Smart doctor with written report missing opening of argument

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: a report missing a letter has had that letter taken out

parts.note: an essay is a written report, as set for homework

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of argument

explanation.surface: A clever physician files a written report that lacks the start of its case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart doctor' looks like a clever physician; smart is the definition, in its sense of well dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressy clothes are elegant and formal, which is what smart means of an outfit.

clue.text: Attacked money, assuming extremities of crime

indicators.note: to assume something is to take it on board, so the money takes letters inside

parts.note: the pound is the currency of Britain

indicators.note: the extremities of a word are its two ends, the first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of crime

explanation.surface: A mugging story: someone went for the cash in a criminal act.
explanation.definitionFit: To pounce is to spring suddenly on prey, so pounced means attacked without warning.
